title: Praxis Special Education: Teaching Students with Learning Disabilities (5383) - 200 Source Questions + 300 Guided Review
description: Contains 200 original source questions, 0 assistant-authored independent practice questions, and 300 source-derived guided-review activities. The assistant audit found 113 distinct independent content kernels. Two 100-item diagnostics, an exact-blueprint 120-item simulation, detailed option feedback, and native learning support for K-12 learning-disabilities specialists.
contentReview: Assistant audit completed: 200 independent-practice items contain 113 distinct content kernels and 87 parallel variants under the normalized test. 300 additional activities are guided reasoning transformations, not independent exam questions. The 500-distinct-question target is not met.
simulationLabel: 120-question Teaching Students with Learning Disabilities simulation
disclaimer: Independent preparation material, not affiliated with or endorsed by ETS. Results are not official forms, scaled scores, pass predictions, licenses, diagnoses, eligibility or placement decisions, legal advice, or substitutes for individualized assessment and current requirements.

domains.label: Development and Characteristics of Students with Learning Disabilities
Planning and Managing the Learning Environment

items.prompt: When interpreting a student’s uneven learning profile, a kindergarten teacher notices that one child reaches several language milestones later than classmates. What is the most appropriate first interpretation?
choices: Broad developmental patterns allow wide variation, so the team should gather multi-source evidence across settings before drawing conclusions.
Falling below the typical classroom average on language milestones establishes a developmental disability that warrants formal eligibility.
The team should assign a provisional disability label promptly so specialized speech-language interventions can begin before gathering family input.
Chronological age norms become uninformative once a child trails classmates, so expectations should be based on informal adult impressions instead.
items.rationale: Milestones provide useful reference points, not stand-alone diagnoses. Educators should document functioning across domains, contexts, and time and involve qualified team members before attributing a pattern to disability. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.
choiceRationales: Correct. Milestones provide useful reference points, not stand-alone diagnoses. Educators should document functioning across domains, contexts, and time and involve qualified team members before attributing a pattern to disability. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.
Classroom averages reflect one peer group rather than a diagnostic standard, and early language variation can stem from experience, exposure, or home-language patterns rather than a disability.
Assigning a provisional disability label before multidisciplinary evaluation and family input bypasses IDEA safeguards and risks misidentifying typical developmental variation as an impairment.
Chronological age remains an essential benchmark for interpreting developmental expectations and selecting age-respectful instructional routines, even when a learner needs targeted supports.

items.prompt: When interpreting a student’s uneven learning profile, a student solves multistep problems during small-group instruction but rarely begins the same work during a noisy whole-class period. What should the teacher examine first?
choices: Conclude that the student has not yet retained the underlying academic skill and re-teach the lesson from the beginning.
Compare task demands, environmental conditions, supports, and performance across both settings.
Lower the academic complexity of the independent assignment so the student can finish without using classroom supports.
Treat the drop in task initiation during the busier period as willful avoidance and add a stricter compliance consequence.
items.rationale: Performance reflects an interaction among learner skills, task demands, supports, and context. Comparing conditions can identify a removable barrier before the team changes expectations or infers a stable trait. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.
choiceRationales: Because the student already demonstrates the skill in the structured setting, the gap points to contextual or support barriers rather than a loss of conceptual understanding.

Correct. Performance reflects an interaction among learner skills, task demands, supports, and context. Comparing conditions can identify a removable barrier before the team changes expectations or infers a stable trait. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.
Reducing academic complexity lowers expectations unnecessarily when the learner has already shown the ability to meet the target under supportive environmental conditions.
Interpreting context-dependent disengagement as intentional defiance overlooks sensory, organizational, or initiation barriers that can be addressed proactively through environmental supports.

items.prompt: When interpreting a student’s uneven learning profile, a teacher wants to understand a learner’s self-regulation needs. Which information is most useful?
choices: A single global behavior rating scale completed by a previous teacher at the start of the school year.
The student’s primary disability eligibility category paired with a general list of typical classroom accommodations.
Current observations of triggers, strategies used, recovery patterns, and successful routines.
Whole-class averages showing how long most classmates sustain independent work without requesting teacher support.
items.rationale: Self-regulation is best understood through specific, current observations of what precedes difficulty, how the learner responds, which strategies help, and whether patterns differ by setting or task. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.
choiceRationales: An outdated global rating summarizes broad impressions from another context and fails to identify the specific triggers, warning signs, and calming strategies relevant to current routines.
Eligibility labels describe broad qualifying criteria rather than individual regulation profiles, so relying on category lists misses the learner’s actual antecedents and effective coping tools.

Correct. Self-regulation is best understood through specific, current observations of what precedes difficulty, how the learner responds, which strategies help, and whether patterns differ by setting or task. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.
Peer-group averages show general classroom norms but do not reveal what overwhelms this individual student or which environmental adjustments help restore engagement.

items.prompt: When interpreting a student’s uneven learning profile, a multilingual learner has difficulty following rapid oral directions in English but demonstrates the task after a peer models it. Which interpretation is best?
choices: Difficulty demonstrating understanding through rapid English oral tasks provides sufficient evidence to suspect an intellectual disability.
Peer modeling and visual representations should be removed during checks so the teacher can measure the student’s true academic mastery.
Information about how the student performs in the home language is outside school accountability and should be set aside during planning.
Language access may affect how knowledge is shown, so gather culturally and linguistically appropriate evidence.
items.rationale: Difference is not disability. The team should distinguish language acquisition and access from disability by using multiple methods, appropriate language supports, and information about performance in the learner’s languages. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.
choiceRationales: Limited proficiency in rapid English instructions reflects second-language processing demands, not impaired intellectual functioning; accurate demonstration via modeling or visuals argues against cognitive deficit.
Stripping away modeling or visual supports confounds English language load with content mastery, making assessment data less valid rather than more accurate.
Home-language performance is crucial evidence for distinguishing language acquisition from disability and helps educators build on concepts the student already understands.

Correct. Difference is not disability. The team should distinguish language acquisition and access from disability by using multiple methods, appropriate language supports, and information about performance in the learner’s languages. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.

items.prompt: When interpreting a student’s uneven learning profile, a middle school student with a learning disability is embarrassed when an adult uses age-inappropriate materials for a functional routine. What principle should guide revision?
choices: Use age-respectful materials while adapting task steps and supports to current learner needs.
Select instructional materials strictly by developmental age estimate so the formatting matches early-childhood readiness charts.
Postpone functional and daily-living instruction until the student achieves independent mastery on grade-level academic standards.
Assign helpful classmates to perform the functional routine for the student so embarrassing instructional materials are unnecessary.
items.rationale: Instruction can be individualized without sacrificing dignity. Materials and contexts should be chronological-age respectful, while prompts, task steps, and response modes are adapted to the learner’s present performance. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.

Delaying essential daily-living instruction until full grade-level mastery denies functional independence and violates the balance between academic access and life-skills preparation.
Having peers complete the routine removes authentic learning opportunities, fosters dependence, and prevents the student from building self-determined functional skills.

items.prompt: When interpreting a student’s uneven learning profile, a student performs a social routine only with one familiar adult. Which plan best promotes generalization?
choices: Continue drilling the skill in the original instructional setting until accuracy stays high across several additional months.
Teach across planned variations in people, materials, and natural settings, then fade prompts.
Introduce multiple unrelated social and communication targets simultaneously so the student practices broader flexibility right away.
End direct instruction once mastery appears in the familiar setting and monitor whether transfer emerges spontaneously over time.
items.rationale: Generalization is more likely when instruction deliberately varies relevant people, materials, and settings, reinforces the skill in natural routines, and gradually transfers stimulus control away from adult prompts. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.
choiceRationales: Over-practicing in one controlled setting with one adult strengthens narrow stimulus control and rarely transfers without deliberate instruction across natural partners and environments.

Correct. Generalization is more likely when instruction deliberately varies relevant people, materials, and settings, reinforces the skill in natural routines, and gradually transfers stimulus control away from adult prompts. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.
Adding unrelated targets at the same time increases cognitive load and interferes with consolidating the specific cue-response link the student needs to transfer.
Hoping for spontaneous transfer—often called train-and-hope—frequently fails for learners who need explicit programming across settings, natural cues, and reinforcement contingencies.

items.prompt: When interpreting a student’s uneven learning profile, a team is writing a learner profile. Which statement is most useful for planning?
choices: The student performs at a low-functioning developmental level across most structured and unstructured school routines.
Because the student has an autism diagnosis, the student prefers fixed classroom schedules and dislikes unexpected changes.
The student completes a two-step visual routine independently and needs one verbal cue when steps change.
The student operates at a developmental stage several years below same-age classmates in daily classroom independence.
items.rationale: Objective descriptions identify a demonstrated strength, a specific condition, and the support needed. Global labels and assumptions based on category do not tell the team what to teach or how to measure change. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.
choiceRationales: Broad deficit labels such as low-functioning are non-specific, lack measurable baseline data, and fail to show what the student can already do or which prompts help.

Correct. Objective descriptions identify a demonstrated strength, a specific condition, and the support needed. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.

items.prompt: When interpreting a student’s uneven learning profile, a learner’s participation drops after a recent family move and change in transportation. How should the school respond?
choices: Attribute the sudden drop in classroom participation to progression of the student’s underlying disability profile.
Recommend moving the student to a more restrictive special education classroom so academic expectations can be reduced.
Keep classroom planning focused on curriculum pacing because housing and transportation factors fall outside school instruction.
Weigh environmental disruptions alongside disability needs and coordinate supports respectfully.
items.rationale: Development and learning are influenced by environmental as well as biological factors. A responsive team gathers context, protects privacy, stabilizes access, and avoids treating a situational change as proof of a new disability need. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.
choiceRationales: Blaming an acute performance drop on an existing disability overlooks clear situational stressors such as disrupted sleep, attendance, or routines that require stabilization supports.

Ignoring major environmental stressors misses actionable school-based resources—such as flexible check-ins, McKinney-Vento coordination, and counseling—that directly affect access to learning.

items.prompt: When interpreting a student’s uneven learning profile, a teacher records one difficult morning and says a student has lost a previously learned skill. What evidence is needed before changing the program?
choices: Gather repeated observations and work samples under representative conditions and compare them with baseline data.
Revise the instructional program right away because the most recent classroom observation reflects the student’s current true level.
Review the student’s disability classification report to confirm whether regression is commonly associated with that label.
Postpone gathering additional evidence until the scheduled annual IEP meeting so classroom routines remain uninterrupted.
items.rationale: A single observation may be affected by health, context, fatigue, or task features. Repeated measures and comparison with baseline information support a more reliable decision about whether performance truly changed. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.
choiceRationales: Correct. A single observation may be affected by health, context, fatigue, or task features. Repeated measures and comparison with baseline information support a more reliable decision about whether performance truly changed. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.
A single low session is vulnerable to fatigue, illness, distraction, or testing glitches and provides insufficient reliability to justify major programmatic changes.

items.prompt: A student with a specific learning disability reads grade-level text accurately but cannot organize written paragraphs. Which response is best?
choices: Deliver uniform remedial instruction across all core academic subjects so the student receives consistent skill reinforcement.
Target the documented area of academic need while preserving strengths in unaffected subjects.
Interpret the persistent academic bottleneck as evidence of broadly limited cognitive ability across every learning domain.
Assign an instructional aide to complete the demanding academic steps so the student can keep pace with class assignments.
items.rationale: Specific learning disabilities can affect particular psychological processes and academic skills unevenly. Instruction should be based on the learner’s actual pattern of strengths and needs, not a global assumption. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.
choiceRationales: Applying blanket remediation across strong subjects wastes instructional time, lowers engagement, and ignores the defining uneven skill profile typical of specific learning disabilities.

Correct. Specific learning disabilities can affect particular psychological processes and academic skills unevenly. Instruction should be based on the learner’s actual pattern of strengths and needs, not a global assumption. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.
Specific learning disabilities affect targeted processing and academic skills rather than overall intellectual capacity, so inferring broad cognitive limits misinterprets the learner’s profile.
Having an adult complete the challenging task prevents skill acquisition, creates prompt dependence, and substitutes completion for specially designed instruction.

items.prompt: A student with a learning disability and autism covers their ears during fire-drill announcements and then misses directions. Which support is most responsive?
choices: Treat covering the ears and missing directions as task refusal and apply standard classroom behavior consequences.
Excuse the student from participating in future schoolwide drills or timed transitions to avoid triggering sensory distress.
Build a predictable warning and accessible cueing routine while teaching the student how to use it.
Continue using loud, unannounced signals without preparation so the student gradually desensitizes through repeated exposure.
items.rationale: Sensory and communication needs can affect access and behavior. A predictable warning, accessible direction, and taught coping or communication response support participation while preserving safety requirements. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.
choiceRationales: Treating sensory overload as willful defiance misreads a neurobiological access barrier and can escalate distress without teaching an effective safety or transition response.
Excluding the student from safety drills or transitions undermines safety preparedness and reduces inclusive participation when proactive sensory supports can enable success.

Correct. Sensory and communication needs can affect access and behavior. A predictable warning, accessible direction, and taught coping or communication response support participation while preserving safety requirements. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.
Unprepared exposure to painful or overwhelming auditory stimuli risks trauma and escalation rather than building self-regulation or reliable response to emergency directions.

items.prompt: A student with a learning disability and ADHD begins work when directions are chunked and a checklist is visible. What does this pattern suggest?
choices: The student already mastered the self-management skills needed and had been choosing not to start earlier assignments.
Adding checklists and interim milestones has lowered the rigor of the grade-level academic standard being assessed.
The student’s uneven project completion reflects limited intellectual understanding of the content rather than self-regulation.
Executive-function scaffolds are strengthening task initiation, planning, and self-monitoring.

items.prompt: A student with a learning disability argues mainly during unpredictable peer-group reading tasks but participates when assigned jobs and steps are explicit. What perspective is most useful?
choices: Analyze interactions among literacy demands, peer roles, expectations, supports, and consequences across contexts.
Expect the same level of arguing across every academic period because the behavior reflects an internal trait.
Conclude that classmates’ reading habits directly caused the student’s underlying specific learning disability.
Replace all collaborative peer-group literacy routines with isolated individual seatwork for the school year.
items.rationale: An ecological and instructional analysis uses the contrast between routines to identify barriers, teach participation and self-advocacy strategies, clarify roles, and monitor both literacy access and behavior.
choiceRationales: Correct. An ecological and instructional analysis uses the contrast between routines to identify barriers, teach participation and self-advocacy strategies, clarify roles, and monitor both literacy access and behavior.
Treating arguing as invariant across classes ignores the student’s documented engagement when peer roles and task steps are explicit.
Peer social interactions do not cause a neurobiological learning disability, and blaming classmates misses modifiable instructional and structural supports.
Eliminating collaborative literacy permanently restricts inclusive peer learning instead of teaching clear roles, scaffolds, and participation routines.

items.prompt: Which evidence best identifies an individualized learning-disability profile for instructional planning?
choices: A single low standardized reading comprehension score collected during one fall screening administration.
Multiple measures of academic skills, error patterns, language context, instruction, response data, and strengths.
General impressions of physical appearance paired with family medical records from early childhood visits.
One general education teacher’s classroom expectations reviewed without student work samples or progress data.
items.rationale: Instructional planning for a learning disability uses converging, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence to identify specific strengths, needs, error patterns, access barriers, and response to explicit instruction.
choiceRationales: A single low reading score cannot map an uneven learning-disability profile, rule out language or instructional factors, or identify error patterns.

Correct. Instructional planning for a learning disability uses converging, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence to identify specific strengths, needs, error patterns, access barriers, and response to explicit instruction.
Physical appearance and early medical records do not document current academic skill patterns, instructional history, or response to targeted teaching.
One teacher’s informal expectations lack objective work samples, error analysis, and cross-setting evidence required for individualized planning.

items.prompt: A student with a learning disability understands grade-level ideas but has difficulty producing clear speech. What is the most appropriate instructional assumption?
choices: Simplify the cognitive complexity of class questions so the student can participate with brief, low-demand responses.
Speak for the student during whole-class discussions so the pacing of the lesson remains smooth for classmates.
Presume competence, support an accessible response mode, and separate vocal output from content mastery.
Require spoken oral answers during formal checks so the student gets daily practice in expressive articulation.
items.rationale: A communication disability can limit how knowledge is expressed without indicating limited understanding. Accessible response modes and adequate wait time help the student demonstrate the intended construct. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.
choiceRationales: Lowering cognitive rigor confuses speech-production barriers with intellectual capacity and deprives the learner of grade-level conceptual challenge.
Answering on the student’s behalf silences the learner’s voice, denies authentic communication practice, and prevents accurate assessment of what the student knows.

Correct. A communication disability can limit how knowledge is expressed without indicating limited understanding. Accessible response modes and adequate wait time help the student demonstrate the intended construct. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.

items.prompt: A student with a learning disability also has visual and motor disabilities. How should the team plan access?
choices: Attach standard classroom accommodations for each separate disability label without trialing how they work together.
Prioritize accommodations for the student’s primary eligibility category while keeping other routines unchanged.
Predict all classroom barriers directly from diagnostic descriptions so lab trials are not necessary before starting.

Collaborative task analysis and trials show how combined access, communication, positioning, and health supports function. Addressing only one eligibility label leaves interacting sensory, motor, or health barriers unaddressed and risks unsafe or inaccessible participation.
Diagnostic categories describe broad patterns, not how a specific learner’s multiple needs interact with particular equipment, lighting, acoustics, and positioning.

items.prompt: A student with dyslexia reads familiar words from memory but struggles to decode new words. Which instruction most directly addresses the need?

Extended independent silent reading time with self-selected books and minimal adult interruption or feedback.
Repeated flashcard drills aimed at memorizing the visual outline of each new grade-level vocabulary word.

Explicit, systematic instruction with modeling, guided practice, cumulative review, and feedback directly addresses these skills. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.
choiceRationales: Correct. Dyslexia commonly involves difficulties with accurate or fluent word recognition, decoding, and spelling. For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.

items.prompt: While developing an individualized program for a student with a learning disability, which present-level statement best supports individualized planning?
choices: Compared with classmates across the grade level, the student performs significantly below expectations in writing.
Across three writing samples, the student wrote a clear topic sentence twice and added supporting details once.

items.prompt: While developing an individualized program for a student with a learning disability, which draft annual IEP goal is written in measurable terms?

Sustaining effort is an inferred internal state rather than a measurable reading skill with an objective accuracy, rate, or consistency standard.

For 5383 preparation, connect the response to the learner’s uneven skill profile, explicit and systematic instruction, appropriate access, culturally and linguistically responsive evidence, and observable progress rather than assuming that a learning-disability label predicts performance.

A goal without a monitoring plan is incomplete for decision making.
